summary: Sporting News compiles a running list of apologies by PGMOL, the body responsible for referees in English football, for incorrect refereeing and VAR decisions in the Premier League. It opens with the 2023/24 season incidents, including Wolves being denied a penalty at Manchester United and a wrongly disallowed Luis Diaz goal in Tottenham 2-1 Liverpool. It then lists earlier errors from 2022 and 2023, covering wrong offside calls, penalties, red cards and disallowed goals.
one_line: A running list of PGMOL apologies for Premier League refereeing and VAR errors, from February 2022 to the Tottenham-Liverpool match of September 30, 2023.
key_facts: Wolves lost 1-0 at Manchester United on August 14, 2023 after being denied a late penalty for Andre Onana's foul on Sasa Kalajdzic, despite a long VAR check.
Jonathan Moss of PGMOL apologised for the Wolves error after the match, which manager Gary O'Neil said he appreciated.
In Tottenham 2-1 Liverpool on September 30, 2023, Luis Diaz's goal was wrongly ruled offside because VAR Darren England ended his check without drawing lines; PGMOL called it a "serious human error".
Liverpool were down to nine men in that match after a red card to Curtis Jones and two bookings for Diogo Jota, and Joel Matip's stoppage-time own-goal gave Tottenham the win.
Chief Refereeing Officer Howard Webb apologised to Brighton after they were denied a penalty in their 2-1 loss at Tottenham on April 8, 2023.
In Arsenal 1-1 Brentford on February 11, 2023, VAR's Lee Mason did not use the right player when checking offside for Brentford's goal; Mikel Arteta said "That wasn't a human error."
John Brooks was taken off VAR duty for two games after drawing the offside line in the wrong place in Crystal Palace 1-1 Brighton, denying Pervis Estupinan a goal.
Aston Villa's 3-1 win over Manchester United on November 6, 2022 included a Lucas Digne free-kick taken with the wall set more than 10 yards behind the ball.
Douglas Luiz was wrongly sent off in Fulham 3-0 Aston Villa on October 20, 2022; Aleksandar Mitrovic was the real instigator of the bust-up.
Gabriel Martinelli's goal was wrongly disallowed in Manchester United 3-1 Arsenal on September 4, 2022 for an alleged Martin Odegaard foul on Christian Eriksen.
Webb's first apology in his new role came after Andy Madley awarded Crystal Palace a wrong penalty against Aston Villa on August 20, 2022.
Mike Riley apologised to Everton after VAR official Chris Kavanagh stuck with the on-field decision not to award a penalty for Rodri's handball in Everton 0-1 Manchester City on February 26, 2022.
